unit.why: An ethical teaching against young men smoking, which frames a short anecdote about R. Shalom of Belz giving up his pipe because it took time from Talmud study.
unit.boundary_note: The homiletic frame (rule ג) on smoking began in the previous division's heading. A brief halakhic report from Ksav Sofer about R. Mordechai Benet follows the anecdote.

stories.start_quote: ושמעתי איך שרבינו הק׳ מהר״ש מבעלז
stories.summary_en: In his youth R. Shalom of Belz saw that he had studied a whole page of Gemara while a youth cleaned and filled his pipe, and he resolved never to smoke again so that the pipe would not take him away from Torah.

tags.why: The anecdote turns on the tsaddik's pipe smoking.
Talmud study is the value he weighs against smoking.
The scene takes place in the study hall.

quotes: לא תבא עוד בפי ומאז והלאה לא לקח אותה מעולם
ומאז והלאה לא לקח אותה מעולם
tags.why: Self-denial of a pleasure for the sake of study.
Illustrates the tsaddik's devotion to study and his self-discipline.
The anecdote sits inside an ethical-homiletic rule against smoking, with verse exegesis and halakhic citations.
The text's declared purpose is moral instruction to young men.

quotes: כי כל הרואה יראה שזה כולו גאות
tags.why: The frame condemns smoking as arrogance.
